newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Amicable says to shed mutuality and float.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Amicable says to shed mutuality and float.

text.p: Life assurer Scottish Amicable said on Thursday it planned to shed its mutual status and float on the London Stock Exchange in three to five years' time.

It said it will pay an initial special bonus of 75 million pounds ($125 million) to policy-holders followed by further benefits at flotation which it said should be substantially higher than a base figure of 200 million pounds.
Scottish Amicable, based in Glasgow and founded in 1826, said in a statement the process would be in two stages and it expects to drop its mutual status on May 1.

Under the plans, the business, staff and operations of the group would be transferred to a new company, Scottish Amicable Life, a 100 percent owned subsidiary of the newly formed Scottish Amicable Holdings.
The first stage involves a deal with reinsurance giant Swiss Re and its affiliate Securitas Capital to provide "substantial financial backing initially totalling 395 million pounds", the group added.
Scottish Amicable's policyholders will first have to give the plans their approval and a special general meeting is expected to be held in March.
It said detailed discussions had already been held with Britain's Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) during the course of developing the proposals.
